title: Many Japanese Parents Don't Find Mealtimes Enjoyable
paragraphs: Eating is usually seen as an enjoyable part of the day. But for many parents of young children in Japan, mealtimes are not very relaxing, according to a new survey.

The survey was done by a research center run by Akachan Honpo, a large Japanese chain of stores for babies and children. In January and February 2026, it asked 1,218 mothers and fathers aged 20 to 49 with children up to three years old about their own meals. The results were shared in August.

The survey found that about 30% of parents were not happy with their mealtime environment. For example, many parents said they cannot eat in a relaxing place or eat at their own speed. Besides the online survey, the researchers also interviewed six parents to learn more about their experiences.

Interestingly, fewer parents had problems with the food itself. Less than 20% said they were unhappy that they could not eat the food they wanted, or food with the flavors they like. This suggests that the main problem is not what parents eat, but how they eat it.
The report also found that sharing childcare was important. In homes where both parents worked together to take care of their children, parents tended to be happier with their meals and their lives.

Other surveys have also found that many Japanese parents have worries about meals. For example, a survey by HugKum, a parenting website, found that more than 90% of parents of children aged 0 to 12 have concerns about their children's eating, such as children not eating or playing with food.
However, the researchers say the survey shows a connection, not a cause.
